coordinates.locator: mean of the centroids of the six OpenStreetMap reactor-building footprints of the Hanbit plant (src:geo-reactors-osm-hanbit-reactors); NEOS paper section 1 for the unit-5 tendon gallery
coordinates.note: Campus-grade: the point is the mean of the six reactor-building centroids (they lie along a ~1.3 km line, 120-650 m from the mean). The NEOS paper puts the detector 23.7 m from the core of unit 5, but no fetched source maps the operator's unit numbers onto the OpenStreetMap buildings, so the hall cannot be placed more precisely; the true position is within about 700 m of this point.
coordinates.quote: The NEOS detector was installed in the tendon gallery of reactor unit 5 of the Hanbit Nuclear Power Complex in Yeonggwang, Korea.

depth_mwe.quote: The minimum overburden with the ground and building structures corresponds to 20 m water equivalent.

name: Hanbit Unit 5 tendon gallery (NEOS)
notes: Distinct from the RENO near/far detector sites, which lie 294 m and ~1.4 km from the reactors.

summary.plain: A gallery under the wall of the reactor containment building at the Hanbit nuclear power complex in Korea, ten metres below ground, where the NEOS detector sat about 24 metres from the core of the unit-5 reactor.
summary.technical: Tendon gallery of Hanbit reactor unit 5, 10 m below ground level directly under the containment-building wall; minimum overburden 20 m.w.e. Marked with a campus-grade plant-centre point.
